title: 2 Climbers Found Dead on Russia’s Second-Highest Mountain Peak
text: 2 Climbers Found Dead on Russia’s Second-Highest Mountain Peak Sep. 23, 2026 Russian Emergencies Ministry Two missing climbers were found dead following a three-day search and rescue operation on one of Russia’s highest mountains in the North Caucasus republic of Kabardino-Balkaria, the Emergency Situations Ministry said Wednesday. The climbers went missing on Sunday while attempting a highly challenging ascent of Mount Dykhtau, which rises 5,200 meters (17,060 feet) above sea level and is the second-highest peak in Russia and Europe after Mount Elbrus. Both failed to contact base camp personnel at their designated time and elevation of 3,800 meters, after which emergency services were alerted. The Emergency Situations Ministry said it planned to dispatch a commercial helicopter to evacuate the bodies. Russian media reported that the climbers had arrived from the cities of Nizhny Novgorod and Tolyatti. Regional law enforcement authorities reportedly opened a preliminary investigation into the deaths. The deaths come after an avalanche on the nearby Mount Mizhirgi killed 17 climbers earlier in September. Read more about: Kabardino-Balkaria , Emergency Situations Ministry , Accidents

title: Russian Military Helicopter Briefly Entered Polish Airspace
text: Russian Military Helicopter Briefly Entered Polish Airspace By Reuters Sep. 23, 2026 A Russian Mi‑8 helicopter. NASA / Bill Ingalls A Russia n military helicopter made a brief incursion into Poland's airspace from the Russia n exclave of Kaliningrad, Polish military officials said Wednesday. The Mi-8 helicopter spent 42 seconds in Polish airspace and entered to a maximum depth of about 300 meters (328 yards), the Polish Army Operational Command said in a post on X. "Fighter aircraft were scrambled, and ground-based forces and assets remained on standby. The nature of the incident indicates that Russia is once again testing the readiness of our air defense," it said. Poland, a NATO member, is on heightened alert for any incursion into its airspace connected with Russia 's war against neighboring Ukraine. The Russia n Embassy in Warsaw did not immediately reply to a Reuters request for comment about the incident. title: 2 Climbers Found Dead on Russia’s Second-Highest Mountain Peak
text: 2 Climbers Found Dead on Russia’s Second-Highest Mountain Peak Sep. 23, 2026 Russian Emergencies Ministry Two missing climbers were found dead following a three-day search and rescue operation on one of Russia’s highest mountains in the North Caucasus republic of Kabardino-Balkaria, the Emergency Situations Ministry said Wednesday. The climbers went missing on Sunday while attempting a highly challenging ascent of Mount Dykhtau, which rises 5,200 meters (17,060 feet) above sea level and is the second-highest peak in Russia and Europe after Mount Elbrus. Both failed to contact base camp personnel at their designated time and elevation of 3,800 meters, after which emergency services were alerted. The Emergency Situations Ministry said it planned to dispatch a commercial helicopter to evacuate the bodies. Russian media reported that the climbers had arrived from the cities of Nizhny Novgorod and Tolyatti. Regional law enforcement authorities reportedly opened a preliminary investigation into the deaths. The deaths come after an avalanche on the nearby Mount Mizhirgi killed 17 climbers earlier in September. Read more about: Kabardino-Balkaria , Emergency Situations Ministry , Accidents

text: Eating garden weeds to survive in Russian-occupied city cut off from food and water Image source, Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets Image caption, Oleshky has been under Russian occupation since 2022 and its people are now trapped By Olga Malchevska Published 24 September 2026 "Two more civilians died last night," says Halia, before her phone connection cuts off. She is trapped in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky, which she says is "constantly shelled" and cut off from food and water. Three days later she tells me the two who were killed were a husband and wife. She knew them well. Ilya Berdnikov, a former official at Russia’s state property management agency Rosimushchestvo, will head Auchan Retail Russia after President Vladimir Putin signed an executive order last week placing it under temporary state management, the newspaper Kommersant reported . Sources familiar with the matter said Auchan Retail Russia’s former CEO Asya Balabay will stay on to manage daily store operations under Berdnikov’s supervision. Denis Isayev, the son of former State Duma lawmaker Rizvangadzhi Isayev, will take over at Lemana Pro, according to Kommersant. As with Auchan, the former CEO of the home improvement chain, previously known as Leroy Merlin, will remain at the company and work with Isayev. news Putin Orders Seizure of U.S. Packaging Maker’s Russian Plant Read more FM Logistic, meanwhile, will be headed by Yevgeny Nenashev, a former housing official in the Moscow region. title: 2 Climbers Found Dead on Russia’s Second-Highest Mountain Peak
text: 2 Climbers Found Dead on Russia’s Second-Highest Mountain Peak Sep. 23, 2026 Russian Emergencies Ministry Two missing climbers were found dead following a three-day search and rescue operation on one of Russia’s highest mountains in the North Caucasus republic of Kabardino-Balkaria, the Emergency Situations Ministry said Wednesday. The climbers went missing on Sunday while attempting a highly challenging ascent of Mount Dykhtau, which rises 5,200 meters (17,060 feet) above sea level and is the second-highest peak in Russia and Europe after Mount Elbrus. Both failed to contact base camp personnel at their designated time and elevation of 3,800 meters, after which emergency services were alerted. The Emergency Situations Ministry said it planned to dispatch a commercial helicopter to evacuate the bodies. Russian media reported that the climbers had arrived from the cities of Nizhny Novgorod and Tolyatti. Regional law enforcement authorities reportedly opened a preliminary investigation into the deaths. The deaths come after an avalanche on the nearby Mount Mizhirgi killed 17 climbers earlier in September. Read more about: Kabardino-Balkaria , Emergency Situations Ministry , Accidents

title: Russian Regions Slowly Reimpose Fuel Purchase Limits Amid Ongoing Refinery Attacks
text: Russian Regions Slowly Reimpose Fuel Purchase Limits Amid Ongoing Refinery Attacks Sep. 23, 2026 Arthur Novosiltsev / Moskva News Agency A growing number of Russian regions have recently seen the reintroduction of fuel rationing measures to combat shortages of gasoline and diesel caused by Ukrainian drone strikes against major oil refineries throughout the country. In the Kaluga region southwest of Moscow, Governor Vladislav Shapsha announced the return of an odd-even system based on vehicle license plate numbers and a ban on sales into portable canisters starting Wednesday. “The lines [at gas stations] are back. This causes reasonable frustration,” Shapsha wrote on Telegram. In Siberia’s Zabaikalsky region, authorities announced a cap of 15 liters (4 gallons) per vehicle on AI-92 and AI-95 gasoline grades across 48 gas stations . Fuel reserves in the region stood at 17,000 metric tons, which are expected to run out in 20 days. Zabaikalsky’s regional government stressed that 106 out of its 249 functioning gas stations were selling fuel without any restrictions. title: Firms Linked to Putin Classmate Win $1.5Bln in Moscow School Meal Contracts, Report Says
text: Firms Linked to Putin Classmate Win $1.5Bln in Moscow School Meal Contracts, Report Says Sep. 23, 2026 Kirill Zykov / Moskva News Agency Four companies linked to a former university classmate of President Vladimir Putin won all 39 contracts to supply meals to Moscow schools from 2026 to 2028, the exiled news outlet Vyorstka reported Wednesday. The awards, worth a combined 126.7 billion rubles ($1.5 billion), show how a lucrative school catering business once held by companies owned by late Wagner mercenary group founder Yevgeny Prigozhin has passed to firms with ties to Ilgam Ragimov, who studied law alongside Putin. The four winning companies were registered in March 2024, less than a year after Prigozhin’s mutiny and death in a plane crash. title: Russian Military Helicopter Briefly Entered Polish Airspace
text: Russian Military Helicopter Briefly Entered Polish Airspace By Reuters Sep. 23, 2026 A Russian Mi‑8 helicopter. NASA / Bill Ingalls A Russia n military helicopter made a brief incursion into Poland's airspace from the Russia n exclave of Kaliningrad, Polish military officials said Wednesday. The Mi-8 helicopter spent 42 seconds in Polish airspace and entered to a maximum depth of about 300 meters (328 yards), the Polish Army Operational Command said in a post on X. "Fighter aircraft were scrambled, and ground-based forces and assets remained on standby. The nature of the incident indicates that Russia is once again testing the readiness of our air defense," it said. Poland, a NATO member, is on heightened alert for any incursion into its airspace connected with Russia 's war against neighboring Ukraine. The Russia n Embassy in Warsaw did not immediately reply to a Reuters request for comment about the incident. It was not immediately clear whether Dud faces criminal charges, but an asterisk marked alongside his entry in the database indicates that he is under criminal investigation. title: Eating garden weeds to survive in Russian-occupied city cut off from food and water
text: Eating garden weeds to survive in Russian-occupied city cut off from food and water Image source, Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets Image caption, Oleshky has been under Russian occupation since 2022 and its people are now trapped By Olga Malchevska Published 24 September 2026 "Two more civilians died last night," says Halia, before her phone connection cuts off. She is trapped in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky, which she says is "constantly shelled" and cut off from food and water. Three days later she tells me the two who were killed were a husband and wife. She knew them well. They were bringing home a bag of food from the closest neighbouring town of Radensk, 23km (14 miles) away, but were unable to get home before a curfew imposed by Russian occupation authorities. They were then killed by a drone. Four separate sources have confirmed the deaths of two civilians carrying food on 20 September. Halia does not want to share their names for fear she might be identified. Her name has been changed to protect her safety. title: Eating garden weeds to survive in Russian-occupied city cut off from food and water
text: Eating garden weeds to survive in Russian-occupied city cut off from food and water Image source, Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets Image caption, Oleshky has been under Russian occupation since 2022 and its people are now trapped By Olga Malchevska Published 24 September 2026 "Two more civilians died last night," says Halia, before her phone connection cuts off. She is trapped in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky, which she says is "constantly shelled" and cut off from food and water. Three days later she tells me the two who were killed were a husband and wife. She knew them well. They were bringing home a bag of food from the closest neighbouring town of Radensk, 23km (14 miles) away, but were unable to get home before a curfew imposed by Russian occupation authorities. They were then killed by a drone. Four separate sources have confirmed the deaths of two civilians carrying food on 20 September. Halia does not want to share their names for fear she might be identified. Her name has been changed to protect her safety. title: Russian Military Helicopter Briefly Entered Polish Airspace
text: Russian Military Helicopter Briefly Entered Polish Airspace By Reuters Sep. 23, 2026 A Russian Mi‑8 helicopter. NASA / Bill Ingalls A Russia n military helicopter made a brief incursion into Poland's airspace from the Russia n exclave of Kaliningrad, Polish military officials said Wednesday. The Mi-8 helicopter spent 42 seconds in Polish airspace and entered to a maximum depth of about 300 meters (328 yards), the Polish Army Operational Command said in a post on X. "Fighter aircraft were scrambled, and ground-based forces and assets remained on standby. The nature of the incident indicates that Russia is once again testing the readiness of our air defense," it said. Poland, a NATO member, is on heightened alert for any incursion into its airspace connected with Russia 's war against neighboring Ukraine. The Russia n Embassy in Warsaw did not immediately reply to a Reuters request for comment about the incident. title: Russian Managers Take Control at Western Companies Seized by the Kremlin
text: Russian Managers Take Control at Western Companies Seized by the Kremlin Sep. 23, 2026 duma.gov.ru Kremlin-backed executives have officially taken control of the Russian operations of French retail giant Auchan, home improvement chain Lemana Pro and French logistics operator FM Logistics. Ilya Berdnikov, a former official at Russia’s state property management agency Rosimushchestvo, will head Auchan Retail Russia after President Vladimir Putin signed an executive order last week placing it under temporary state management, the newspaper Kommersant reported . Sources familiar with the matter said Auchan Retail Russia’s former CEO Asya Balabay will stay on to manage daily store operations under Berdnikov’s supervision. Denis Isayev, the son of former State Duma lawmaker Rizvangadzhi Isayev, will take over at Lemana Pro, according to Kommersant. As with Auchan, the former CEO of the home improvement chain, previously known as Leroy Merlin, will remain at the company and work with Isayev. news Putin Orders Seizure of U.S. Packaging Maker’s Russian Plant Read more FM Logistic, meanwhile, will be headed by Yevgeny Nenashev, a former housing official in the Moscow region.
